election-intro.text: Hi, I'm Olive! Today's little big question: what is an election? It's how people in a country choose who gets to make the rules for a while.

election-outro.text: People vote differently because they care about different things, and that is okay. If your class had a vote, what would you choose?

climate-intro.text: Our planet wears a blanket of air. Some of the things we burn make that blanket thicker, so the Earth holds on to more heat.

climate-outro.text: Scientists, families and whole countries are working on it, and they don’t always agree on how. What would you try first?

war-intro.text: This one can feel scary, so let's go slowly. Sometimes countries disagree about land or safety, and talking stops working.

war-outro.text: Lots of people are working hard to help and to make peace. If you feel worried, talking to a grown-up you trust really helps.

inequality-intro.text: Some families have lots of money and some have very little. Where you are born, and the chances you get, can make a big difference.

inequality-outro.text: People have different ideas about what is fair. What do you think fair looks like?

why-are-ukraine-and-russia-fighting-intr.text: This can feel scary, so let's go slowly. Two countries, Ukraine and Russia, are fighting—and we're wondering why.

why-are-ukraine-and-russia-fighting-outr.text: People see this differently, and many grown-ups are working to keep everyone safe. If you feel worried, talking to a grown-up you trust can help—what do you think could help people get along again?
